- **Plan:** Superior HealthPlan (Ambetter), Commercial/ACA, Texas
- **Reference number:** POC-DDD103990C-51911
- **Date of denial notice:** 2026-08-14
- **Service denied:** Shoulder labral / instability repair, CPT 29806
- **Requesting surgeon:** Lindqvist, MD, orthopedic surgery

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for shoulder labral / instability repair (CPT 29806), denied on 2026-08-14 under reference number POC-DDD103990C-51911. The notice states that the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision.

The criteria I am addressing come from the plan's own published guideline, the **2026 Evolent Clinical Guidelines – Musculoskeletal Surgery** (https://www1.radmd.com/sites/default/files/2026-05/2026%20Evolent%20Musculoskeletal%20Surgery%20Guidelines.pdf). Every quotation below is taken word for word from that document. My surgeon has documented that this procedure is needed, and the records already in the plan's possession line up with the guideline's requirements point by point.

---

## What my records show

- Twelve months of recurrent episodes of shoulder instability with apprehension.
- **Three anterior dislocations** since my symptoms began; the most recent was reduced in the emergency department.
- **Supervised physical therapy** focused on rotator cuff and scapular stabilizer strengthening, with activity modification: 2026-05-05 to 2026-07-14, **10 weeks, 16 visits completed**, documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- **NSAIDs for 6 months** during flares. No injection was given, as an injection is not indicated for instability.
- **MR arthrogram of the shoulder, 2026-07-01:** anteroinferior labral tear (Bankart lesion) with a small Hill-Sachs lesion; glenoid bone loss under 10 percent; rotator cuff intact.
- **Examination:** positive apprehension and relocation tests; increased anterior translation on load-and-shift; full strength.
- **Function:** I avoid overhead reaching and I cannot return to work lifting.
- No active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, non-smoker.

---

## The plan's criteria, matched to my records

**The guideline states:**

> "History of an acute event of instability (subluxation or dislocation) or acute onset of pain following activity"

My records document three anterior dislocations since my symptoms began, the most recent reduced in the emergency department.

**The guideline states:**

> "Recurrent instability (two or more episodes of subluxation or dislocation)"

I have had three anterior dislocations, which is more than the two episodes this criterion describes.

**The guideline states:**

> "Clinical exam findings demonstrate positive apprehension test, positive relocation test, positive labral grind test, or objective laxity with pain"

and

> "Physical examination findings demonstrate positive apprehension test, positive relocation test, positive labral grind test, or objective laxity with pain (PE is not required if there has been a recent episode of instability or there is a radiographic evidence of any prior dislocation)"

My examination documents a positive apprehension test and a positive relocation test, along with increased anterior translation on load-and-shift.

**The guideline states:**

> "Labral tear/Bankart lesion on MRI or CT imaging"

and

> "MRI evidence of a labral tear with or without bony Bankart fracture of the glenoid. Cases with a history of frank anterior dislocations without MRI evidence of a labrum tear will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis."

My MR arthrogram of 2026-07-01 shows an anteroinferior labral tear (Bankart lesion) with a small Hill-Sachs lesion, glenoid bone loss under 10 percent, and an intact rotator cuff. This is imaging evidence of exactly the lesion the criterion names, and it accompanies a documented history of anterior dislocations.

**The guideline states:**

> "Symptoms of pain, catching/popping, or instability"

My records document twelve months of recurrent instability episodes with apprehension, avoidance of overhead reaching, and inability to return to work lifting.

---

## On the reason given for the denial

The denial rests on conservative treatment. The plan's guideline contains this requirement:

> "Failure of at least 12 weeks of non-operative treatment (unless presenting as a traumatic tear in a competitive athlete at any level) that includes any TWO of the following:"

That sentence ends in a colon and introduces a list of treatment types that was not reproduced in the excerpt available to me. The guideline also contains a separate requirement:

> "Failure of at least 6 months of formal physical therapy and activity modification"

I want to be straightforward with the plan about what my chart says. My supervised physical therapy course ran 10 weeks, from 2026-05-05 to 2026-07-14, with 16 visits completed and documented in the discharge note. That course was paired with activity modification throughout and with NSAIDs taken over a 6-month period during flares. An injection was not given because an injection is not indicated for instability. So my non-operative care was not a brief trial: it was a structured, supervised program of two different treatment types, carried out over months, and it did not stop my shoulder from dislocating.

I am also asking the plan to clarify which criteria it actually applied. The guideline sets out more than one set of criteria for shoulder instability surgery, including a set introduced by the line:

> "Bankart repair of an acute labral tear may be necessary when all the following criteria are met:"

and separate criteria addressing recurrent instability, posterior labral findings, and instability without traumatic dislocation, such as:

> "Individual has recurrent instability due to hyperlaxity or mobility and no traumatic dislocation"

My presentation is traumatic, recurrent anterior instability with three documented dislocations and an imaging-confirmed Bankart lesion. The excerpts of the guideline available to me do not show that the 12-week and 6-month conservative-care requirements attach to that presentation rather than to the other pathways, and the plan's notice does not identify which criterion set was used or which specific element was found unmet. I am asking the plan to state that on reconsideration, so that I can respond to the actual standard being applied. If the plan relied on a duration requirement, I ask it to identify the criterion set that requirement sits in and explain why it governs a shoulder with three documented dislocations and an MR arthrogram–confirmed Bankart lesion.

Finally, my records show no finding of the kind the guideline lists here:

> "No radiographic evidence of degenerative disease (e.g., posterior glenoid cartilage loss, subchondral glenoid cysts, mucoid degeneration of labrum, narrowing of joint space with posterior humeral head subluxation on axillary x-ray or axial MRI images)"

My imaging reports a labral tear, a small Hill-Sachs lesion, glenoid bone loss under 10 percent, and an intact rotator cuff.

---

## What I am asking for

I ask that Superior HealthPlan (Ambetter):

1. Overturn the denial of CPT 29806 and authorize the shoulder labral / instability repair requested by Dr. Lindqvist;
2. If the denial is maintained, identify in writing the specific criterion set and the specific criterion within the 2026 Evolent Clinical Guidelines – Musculoskeletal Surgery that my records were found not to meet; and
3. Have this appeal reviewed by a physician in orthopedic surgery.

I am submitting this appeal within the timeframe stated in my denial notice, which says the appeal must be received within 180 days of the notice date, by **2027-02-10**. I am sending it to the appeal address printed on that denial letter. I understand I may also file through ambetterhealth.com by selecting Texas and using the state's appeal or grievance form, or by calling the number on my member ID card.

Please contact me at the phone number or email above if anything further is needed. I am happy to have additional records sent directly from Dr. Lindqvist's office or from my physical therapy provider.

Thank you for taking another look at this.

Sincerely,

**Sawyer Hayes**
